text: Missing bases tab: the Scriptmix "Missing Component Bases" (Scripts/Components/Missing Bases.py). Checks every component on every master against the glyphs and master layers of the font and lists each component whose base is missing: the composite, its master, the missing base and the problem ("glyph missing", "no layer" or "component without a base name"). Rows are sorted by missing base, as the original tree grouped them. Choosing a row shows the composite in the TGlyph preview; Select affected glyphs selects every listed composite in the Font window. text: Nested tab: the Scriptmix "Nested Components" (Scripts/Components/Nested Finder.py). Lists every component whose base glyph is itself a composite, on the chosen masters of the selected glyphs or of the whole font, then unnests each by one level: the base's inner components and own contours replace it, placed with the outer transform, so the glyph looks the same. The original's planner ( nested_changes ) is kept verbatim; the plan, blocked rows, auto-layer refusal, stale check and write are Component Studio's reviewed ComponentPanel ( component_writer.EjectEditor(unlock=False) , as the original). "Glyphs": Selected glyphs (default) or Whole font (re-reads the font, as the original's reload); "Masters": all masters by default, as the original. Unnest writes the listed rows as one Component Audit: unnest components <subject> Undo step through AppShell.history on the listed layers, retaining the removed components, then reads them back. Auto layers are listed and never edited; a glyph that owns an auto layer or is a base of one refuses the batch (no opt-in, as in the original).

text: Build tab (Build From Recipes, with Dump Component Recipes as "Dump from selection"). The original's rules are kept unchanged ( Line , Result , parse , data_tool , build , check_lines ): one recipe per line, target = base + mark@anchor ( @acute without brackets names both anchors, @acute[_acute] ); # starts a comment. Check runs FontLab's own builder ( build_glyph ) as a dry run on every line and master; it does not run on open, because the builder can refresh glyph data. A line with NUL, no-break space or line/paragraph separators is refused; a target that owns auto layers or is a base of an auto composite is refused (no opt-in, as in the original). "Masters": current master (default) or all; "Replace existing layers" is off by default. Build is enabled only after Check with every row ready; any change asks for Check again. Build keeps the original's builder route. The empty master layers the builds need are added first as ONE Component Studio: add master layers <subject> Undo step through AppShell.history . Each layer is then built by FontLab's build_glyph data tool with auto_layer=False , as in the original; that tool records its own history, so AppShell.history cannot wrap it and the builder's Undo is FontLab's (native history is qualified in T29). A new glyph is built on its first master; press Build again for the others. "Dump from selection" (Dump Component Recipes) only reads: it captures the selected Font/Glyph-window layers and shows their base+base=glyph recipes verbatim in a read-only box (copy it from there); it writes nothing and opens no history. The dump format is the original's and is not the Build syntax, so it is never pasted into the recipe editor.

text: Decompose tab (Decompose, Decompose Named Components, Decompose Serif Components). The three originals become the three "Components" scopes of one tab; each scope keeps its original's planner, editor, master default and texts: All components (Decompose, decompose_changes ): every component of the selected glyphs becomes the parts of its base glyph, one level per press (" (nested: press again)"); a base that cannot be copied is a red row and refuses the batch. Masters default: current master. Named component (Decompose Named Components, make_plan ): only components whose source is the exact name typed; the whole subtree is flattened into independent outlines. Refused glyphs, missing, automatic, locked or service layers and copy problems are listed as "kept: ..." rows and do not block the other rows. Copies are made on Apply, before history. Masters default: all masters. Serif components (Decompose Serif Components, changes ): only components whose base name starts with "Serif". Masters default: current master. New contours are unlocked ( EjectEditor(unlock=True) ). Auto layers are listed and kept; a glyph that owns auto layers or is a base of one is refused (no opt-in, as in the originals). Apply writes the listed decomposition as one Component Studio: decompose ... <subject> Undo step and hands FontLab each removed component with its data and builder ( retain ); Edit > Undo of removed components depends on FontLab (fl#7641, qualified natively in T29). Credits: Decompose Named Components is an independent behaviour rewrite after Fernando Díaz & Reset Type Studio, Glyphs-Scripts (Apache-2.0); Decompose Serif Components after Pedro Arilla, glyphs-scripts (Apache-2.0). "Action": Set location (default) or Reset to current layer; "Components": Selected components or All components in selected glyphs (default); "Source": an optional exact source name; "Masters": all masters (default). text: Create empty placeholder glyphs from typed glyph names or characters, on every master. What it does: Type or paste glyph names and characters, separated by spaces, commas or new lines. The script creates one empty glyph per entry, with a layer on every master and the chosen advance width. A single non-ASCII character becomes uniXXXX (or uXXXXX) and gets that code point. A name of that form also gets its code point, unless another glyph has it already. ASCII tokens are glyph names: A stays A; & and 1 are invalid names. How it works: A small non-modal panel shows a live table: the name, the code point and what will happen. Existing glyphs, repeated entries and invalid names are listed and skipped. Create checks the font again. FontLab's own Add Glyph command makes each new glyph with a layer on every master, the advance width and the code point (shared module fly.ap.glyphs.creation). After the write the script reads every new glyph back, and checks that no automatic glyph of the font changed. Why this design: - Placeholders let you build features, classes, kerning groups and test strings before the drawings exist. Unlike Font > Add Glyphs, the panel takes characters directly, previews every name and code point, and skips what exists instead of asking. - An existing glyph is never overwritten, and a code point that another glyph has is never assigned twice. - FontLab's text conversion can change some characters, so the script refuses text with NUL, no-break space or the Unicode line and paragraph separators instead of creating changed names. - A code point write needs an active Font window and no open Glyph window, as every Unicode writer of this menu does. Create discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). - FontLab can rebuild an automatic glyph when a new name appears. When the font has automatic glyphs without a recipe whose names share a dotted suffix with a new name (a new e.sc and eacute.sc), the row shows "may rebuild auto ..." and is skipped unless you tick "Create even if FontLab may rebuild these auto glyphs". A change of the text clears the tick. - Each new glyph is recorded as its own Undo step. How to use: Open a font and activate its Font window. Run the script. Type the names or characters, set the advance width, check the table and press Create. Benefit: A complete glyph set skeleton, named and encoded, in seconds. Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (generate_placeholder_glyphs.py, "Placeholder Glyphs").

text: Create small-cap glyphs (h.sc, a.sc, ...) from the selected capitals. What it does: For each selected capital the script creates a small-cap glyph on every master: H becomes h.sc, H.ss01 becomes h.sc.ss01. The outline is scaled by separate horizontal and vertical factors; the advance width is scaled horizontally. The capitals do not change. How it works: A non-modal panel lists every selected glyph with its new name, or the reason why it is skipped. Create checks the font again. FontLab's own Add Glyph command makes each new glyph with its master layers and widths (rounded half up). Then one step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs adds the scaled copies to all new layers. The copy keeps node names and raw node flags, which a FontLab contour copy can drop (fl#8569). After the write the script reads every new layer back, and checks that no automatic glyph of the font changed. The creation, the contour copy and the panel are shared (fly.ap.glyphs.copies, fly.ap.contours.copy). Copy limits: Anchors are not copied. Add the required anchors to the new glyphs before building accented composites. Only node names and raw node flags are repaired (fl#8569); selection is cleared. Other node properties and contour names are not repaired. Copied contours are merged into one element; source element names and notes are not copied. Why this design: - The name is the lowercase base plus ".sc", the usual naming for the smcp and c2sc features. - A larger horizontal than vertical factor keeps vertical stems relatively heavier, so the small caps do not look too light at once. The result is a starting point for drawing, not finished small caps. - A capital needs a layer with contours on every master, with no components and no automatic layer. Otherwise it is listed and skipped, so the new glyphs stay compatible across masters. Accented capitals are usually components: build their small caps from the new bases. - A target name that exists is never overwritten. Create discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). - FontLab can rebuild an automatic glyph when a new name appears. When the font has automatic glyphs without a recipe whose names carry the new suffix (such as eacute.sc), the row shows "may rebuild auto ..." and is skipped unless you tick "Create even if FontLab may rebuild these auto glyphs". Use selection clears the tick. - Each new glyph is recorded as its own Undo step, and the outlines as one more Undo step. How to use: Select capitals in the Font window. Run the script. Set the horizontal and vertical scale, check the table and press Create. Benefit: A compatible set of small caps to refine, in every master, in one step. Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (generate_small_caps.py, "Small Caps from Capitals").

text: Create tabular (.tf) copies of the selected figures, with one shared width per master. What it does: For each selected figure (zero to nine, also with a suffix such as one.osf) the script creates a new glyph with ".tf" added to the name, on every master. In each master all new glyphs get one advance width: the widest selected figure of that master plus an extra amount. The figure outline is copied and centred in that width. The source figures do not change. How it works: A non-modal panel lists every selected glyph with its new name, or the reason why it is skipped. Create checks the font again. FontLab's own Add Glyph command makes each new glyph with its master layers and the shared widths. Then one step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs adds the centred copies to all new layers. The centring keeps the outline on whole units; an odd unit of white space goes to the right side. The copy keeps node names and raw node flags, which a FontLab contour copy can drop (fl#8569). After the write the script reads every new layer back, and checks that no automatic glyph of the font changed. The creation, the contour copy and the panel are shared (fly.ap.glyphs.copies, fly.ap.contours.copy). Copy limits: Anchors are not copied. Add the required anchors to the new glyphs before building accented composites. Only node names and raw node flags are repaired (fl#8569); selection is cleared. Other node properties and contour names are not repaired. Copied contours are merged into one element; source element names and notes are not copied. Why this design: - New glyphs, not changed figures: proportional and tabular figures can then live side by side, as the OpenType tnum feature expects. To make the existing figures tabular in place, use Metrics > Tabular Width. - A figure needs a layer with contours on every master, with no components and no automatic layer. Otherwise the figure is listed and skipped, so the new glyphs stay compatible across masters. - A target name that exists is never overwritten. - Create discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). - FontLab can rebuild an automatic glyph when a new name appears. When the font has automatic glyphs without a recipe whose names carry the new suffix, the row shows "may rebuild auto ..." and is skipped unless you tick "Create even if FontLab may rebuild these auto glyphs". Use selection clears the tick. - Each new glyph is recorded as its own Undo step, and the outlines as one more Undo step. How to use: Select the figures in the Font window. Run the script. Set the extra width, check the table and press Create. Narrow figures such as one can then need redrawing in their wider space. Benefit: A complete, compatible set of tabular figures to refine, in one step. Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (generate_tabular_copies.py, "Tabular Figure Copies").

text: Turn the selected glyphs into outlined (hollow) letters of a chosen line width. What it does: For each selected glyph and chosen master, the script replaces the contours of the layer with a ring of the chosen line width, centred on the old outline. The advance width does not change. How it works: A non-modal panel lists every glyph and master with its contour count, or the reason why the layer is skipped. Apply first builds every ring: Qt's path stroker draws the contours with round joins and caps, the script turns the stroke into closed FontLab contours (cubic handles stay cubic), and FontGate's Remove Overlap cleans the small loops that the stroker leaves inside corners. Then it writes all layers in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs: each old contour element is removed and the ring is added as one new element. Images and empty elements stay in the layer. After the write it counts the contours again and reports any difference. The path-to-contour step and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.copy, fly.ap.contours.selection.panel.model). Why this design: - FontLab has no Python call that strokes an outline, so the script uses the Qt stroker and FontLab's own overlap removal. FontGate puts the result on the integer grid. - The geometry is built before history starts, so a failed stroke never leaves a half-edited layer. - Layers with components are skipped: the components would stay filled. Locked layers are skipped too. Element names and notes of the old outline do not carry over to the ring. - Automatic layers and glyphs with automatic layers are never edited. A base of automatic composites is skipped unless you tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway": FontLab then rebuilds those composites, can drop their anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore them. - Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Set the line width, choose the current master or all masters, check the table and press Outline. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Benefit: An inline or outline style starts from the real drawing, in every master, in one step. Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (generate_outline_effect.py, "Outline Effect").

text: Add a shifted copy of the outline behind each selected glyph, as its own element. What it does: For each selected glyph and chosen master, the script copies the contours of the layer, moves the copy by a horizontal and a vertical offset, and puts it behind the outline as a new element named "shadow". The original outline and the advance width do not change. How it works: A non-modal panel lists every glyph and master with its contour count, or the reason why the layer is skipped. Apply reads the font again and writes all layers in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs. The copy is made from each contour with its element transform applied; FontLab can drop node names and raw node flags in a contour copy (fl#8569), so the script copies them back and clears the selection bit. After the write it checks that every layer starts with the shadow element and reports any difference. The contour copy and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.copy, fly.ap.contours.selection.panel.model). Copy limits: Only node names and raw node flags are repaired (fl#8569); selection is cleared. Other node properties and contour names are not repaired. Copied contours are merged into one element; source element names and notes are not copied. Why this design: - A separate element is easy to recolour, move or delete as one unit, and a layer font workflow can split it into shadow glyphs. Filled together with the outline it gives an extruded silhouette. - Layers with components are skipped: a copy of the contours alone would not be the full glyph. Locked layers and layers that already hold a shadow element are skipped too. - Automatic layers and glyphs with automatic layers are never edited. A base of automatic composites is skipped unless you tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway": FontLab then rebuilds those composites, can drop their anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore them. - Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). The panel binds to the font that was current when it opened. How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Set the offsets, choose the current master or all masters, check the table and press Add Shadow. The panel stays open; press "Use selection" after you select other glyphs. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Benefit: Shadowed or extruded display styles start from the real outline in one step, and the shadow stays a separate element. Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (generate_shadow.py, "Shadow Copy").

text: Run FontLab's PostScript autohinter on the selected glyphs, in one or all masters. What it does: For each selected glyph and chosen master, the script runs FontLab's own autohinter on the layer. It works from the font's hinting settings (alignment zones and standard stems). The table shows the horizontal and vertical hint counts before and after. FontLab's source does not touch TrueType instructions here. How it works: A non-modal panel lists every glyph and master with its hint counts, or the reason why the layer is skipped. Apply reads the font again and calls the native flLayer.autohint() on every planned layer, all in one Undo step through the shared module fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs. Read-back reports a layer that has an outline but no PostScript hints after the call. The hint counts and the panel are shared (fontlabapp.hints.postscript, fontlabapp.contours.selection.panel.model). Native call caveat: FontLab's source shows that autohint switches the package master temporarily, writes hinting options and stored hinting data, and can attach hints as node links. These effects extend beyond the notified layers; the script does not check them. TrueType instructions are separate. Why this design: - The hints come from FontLab's own autohinter, not from a script algorithm. - The script adds what the menu command does not: every master in one step, a count of hints before and after, and one Undo step. - Automatic layers and glyphs with automatic layers are never edited. A base of automatic composites is skipped unless you tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway": the change notification makes FontLab rebuild those composites, which can drop their anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore them. Locked layers and layers without contours are skipped. - Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). How to use: Set the alignment zones and standard stems in Font Info first. Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Choose the current master or all masters, check the table and press Autohint. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Benefit: A whole selection gets fresh PostScript hints in every master, with the counts in view, in one step. Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (hints_autohint.py, "Autohint Selected Layers").

text: Remove PostScript stem hints from the selected glyphs, horizontal and/or vertical. What it does: For each selected glyph and chosen master, the script removes the horizontal hints, the vertical hints or both from the layer. FontLab's source does not touch plain guidelines or TrueType instructions here. The table shows the hint counts before and after. How it works: A non-modal panel lists every glyph and master with its hint counts, or the reason why the layer is skipped. A layer without hints in the chosen directions is listed and skipped. Apply reads the font again and calls the native flLayer.removeHints(horizontal, vertical) on every planned layer, all in one Undo step through the shared module fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs. After the write it counts the hints again and reports any layer that still has hints in a chosen direction. The hint counts and the panel are shared (fontlabapp.hints.postscript, fontlabapp.contours.selection.panel.model). Why this design: - The removal is FontLab's own call, so hints are removed exactly as the menu command removes them. - The script adds what the menu command does not: every master in one step, one direction only, the counts in view and one Undo step. - Automatic layers and glyphs with automatic layers are never edited. A base of automatic composites is skipped unless you tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway": the change notification makes FontLab rebuild those composites, which can drop their anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore them. Locked layers are skipped. - Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Tick the directions, choose the current master or all masters, check the table and press Remove Hints. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Benefit: Clean hint-free layers before a new autohint pass or a TrueType-only export, in every master, in one step. Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (hints_remove.py, "Remove PostScript Hints").

text: Kerning Batch Clamp tab: Scriptmix Kerning Cutoff ("Kerning Cutoff"). What: clamp every master's explicit kerning to the inclusive range -250 to 100 ( kerning.cutoff.LOWER / UPPER ). As in the original there are no options and no current-master subset: all masters, glyph pairs, class pairs and both mixed exception kinds keep their typed identities, values on a limit stay, existing zero stays, and an absent pair is never added. The plan is the shared kerning.cutoff.plan , unchanged, on a typed snapshot. The original ran immediately; here the table lists every clamped pair first and Apply writes exactly that set as one Kerning Batch: Clamp kerning on <masters> Undo step, then reports each master's count as the original printed it. text: Kerning Batch Copy masters tab: Scriptmix Copy Between Masters ("Copy Kerning Between Masters"). What: copy one master's explicit pairs (From, default the current master) to the ticked target masters, optionally scaled (0–400 %, one decimal, default 100 %, halves away from zero), in one of three modes: Replace all pairs (target pairs absent from the source are deleted), Add missing pairs only, or Overwrite matching pairs, keep others. The plan is the shared kerning.edit.model.copy_plan / summary , unchanged; explicit zero and absence stay distinct. The confirmation is the original's: the "To masters" table shows each target's Pairs now, Added, Changed and Removed counts, and Copy is enabled only when a target is ticked and the plan changes something; there is no modal box (the original had none). Copy writes exactly the displayed plan as one Kerning Batch: Copy kerning from <source> to <targets> Undo step. Used by fontlabapp.studios.kerning_batch (tab builder).

text: Kerning Batch Punctuation tab: Scriptmix Unbundle Punctuation Kerning. What: turn inherited (class) values involving the selected glyphs into explicit glyph-pair exceptions on the current master (default) or all masters. Class definitions, class pairs and every existing explicit glyph pair (zero included) stay. "Unicode punctuation only" (on by default) keeps glyphs outside the Unicode P* categories; an unencoded alternate uses its base-name glyph's code points (read from the Fontport font, never fgGlyph ). An ambiguous partner keeps only that pair; a master with invalid class members is named and kept; invalid numeric data on any master keeps the whole font (the writer validates numeric history font-wide). The table lists every planned pair and every kept message (first 500 rows shown); Add Exceptions writes exactly the planned pairs as one Kerning Batch: Add exceptions for <n> glyphs on <masters> Undo step. "Use selection" re-reads the Font window selection. is_punctuation , expand , numeric_problem , master_problem and Row are the original bodies; only the two Fly imports in the last two now read the same App modules through core.scripting.kerning_tool_backends . Independent behaviour rewrite after Simon Cozens, Unbundle Punctuation Kerning.py, MIT. Repository: https://github.com/simoncozens/GlyphsScripts . No code copied. Used by fontlabapp.studios.kerning_batch (tab builder).

What: one master is MasterData(pairs, groups) in UFO key space (classes are public.kern1.<name> on the left side and public.kern2.<name> on the right). These functions find class sides, effective values and the record an edit targets, plan deletes, compute Kern To Max and the Steal gap value, parse preview text into pairs, and list a glyph's pairs and group peers. text: Kerning Studio state: per-master reads and per-master kerning writes. What: Studio takes one snapshot of every master's pairs and classes from the live package ( fontlabapp.fontui.kerning_snapshot ; reading changes nothing) and keeps the master the preview shows. Every write is one fontlabapp.fontui.write_kerning call: {master: {pair: value or None}} on any masters, one "Kerning Studio: <action> <pair>" Undo step, checked against the snapshot it was planned from and read back (Issue 235 §1.3/§1.4). Why: The selected (preview) master is the write target; "Delete pair on all masters" and the per-master grid write several masters in one step, as the Scriptmix scripts did.
